title: Quicksplice: compact customer signal & mini feature catalog (Mar 2027)
body:
Purpose: quick, compact roll-up of recent customer signals (Feb–Mar 2027) focused on low-effort, high-impact fixes and experimental probes. This is intentionally terse — use as a sprint-ready intake for Eng + Product triage.

Context and how I collected these: rapid sampling from support threads, CSM weekly notes, two recorded customer calls (acct A, acct B), and internal chat snippets. Not a full VOC extraction; this is a bias-prioritized note: signals that repeatedly show up AND have clear actionable probes.

Topline micro-themes (counts are rough mentions across sources):
- Confusing model-fallback behavior (mentions: ~18): customers see silent fallback to smaller/quantized model and notice quality drops.
- High variance in token billing vs expected (mentions: ~12): customers surprised by invisible prefix tokens and streaming tokens count.
- Batch latency spikes under mixed workloads (mentions: ~9): endpoints with mixed short/long sequences see occasional 2–3x latency bursts.
- Need for deterministic eval hooks (mentions: ~7): customers want automated eval runs tied to rollouts so they can block bad regressions.
- Embeddings drift for long-term corpora (mentions: ~6): drift over weekly ingestion cycles causing search ranking changes.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We keep losing output quality — sometimes it just switches and responses are worse; we only notice when users complain."
- "Billing blobs don't match what our integration expects — we can't map tokens to call logic easily."
- "Latency is fine at low QPS, but mid-day we get big stalls and our UI times out."

Priority quick fixes (P0 / P1 / P2) — recommended probes and owners
1) P0 — Explicit fallback logging and telemetry (owner: eng-infra / SRE)
   - Problem: silent fallback to cheaper variants; customers lose visibility and get degraded outputs.
   - Probe: add a per-request 'fallback_reason' field in logs + optional response header 'x-redwood-fallback' when fallback occurs. Expose in Console trace UI and in API response when ?debug=1.
   - Success metric: decrease in "unexpected quality drop" tickets by 50% within 4 weeks (CS tracked).
   - Quick implementation notes: toggle behind feature-flag; small change in routing layer. JIRA: JIRA-2345 (placeholder).

2) P0 — Token accounting debug view (owner: product-hosted-api)
   - Problem: customers confused by prefix/KV/cache token accounting.
   - Probe: console mini-view showing per-request token breakdown (prompt, prefix, cache-hit delta, streaming overhead). Add downloadable CSV for billing reconciliation.
   - Success metric: <10 follow-up reconciliation tickets for pilot customers.
   - Risks: exposing internal charge rules might require legal review — loop in finance.

3) P1 — Mixed-workload batching policy tweak experiment (owner: serving-runtime)
   - Problem: spikes from mixed sequence-length batching.
   - Probe: two-week A/B: route 50% of tenant traffic through sequence-length-aware micro-batcher (limits packing when long sequences present). Measure p50/p95 latency, tail latency and token throughput.
   - Monitoring hooks: attach trace IDs to sample slow requests, link to Console traces.

4) P1 — Eval-as-a-gate PoC for rollouts (owner: product/optimize)
   - Idea: add a small eval harness that runs a canonical prompt set (customer-provided or Redwood seed set) against candidate versions before canary promotion.
   - Probe: run nightly for 5 pilot tenants; if quality delta exceeds threshold, block automated rollouts.

5) P2 — Embedding-stability doc + small retrain cadence recommendation (owner: applied-ml)
   - Problem: customers see drift in vector scores over time as corpora change.
   - Probe: produce a 1-pager with best-practice: periodic reindexing cadence, embedding normalization, and contrastive monitoring.

Low-effort UX patches (can ship in sprint)
- Add tooltips to Console 'Model variant' explaining quantization/expected quality delta.
- Expose short-form webhook for billing events: send token-breakdown on demand (opt-in).
- Add "why this fallback" quick link in trace view to surface fallback policy rules.

Open questions / things to validate with customers
- How many customers would opt into verbose token-breakdown in API responses vs only in Console? (ask via short poll)
- For eval-as-gate: do customers prefer Redwood-managed canonical set or uploading their own test prompts?
- For batching tweak: what is the average ratio of short:long sequences per tenant? need infra metrics.

Risks and compliance notes
- Token-breakdown and per-request debug data could leak PII if not redacted—coordinate with security for redaction rules.
- Fallback headers that reveal model variants could be problematic for customers who want abstraction; make opt-in.

Suggested next steps (fast path)
1) Quick sync (30 min) with SRE, serving-runtime lead, Product-hosted-api this week to agree on telemetry fields and owners.
2) Draft JIRA tickets for P0 items with acceptance criteria and small mockups for Console.
3) Identify 3 pilot customers (CS) who already reported these issues and invite them to opt into pilots.
4) Legal/security review queued for token debug export.

Notes to self / fragments for follow-up
- Could we add a small retention tag for fallback events so we can answer "when did X start" for customers?
- Consider a single multi-tenant "repro harness" that replays traces to test new batching strategies.
- Make sure billing hooks align with finance's monthly billing export.

Appendix: quick link map (internal)
- Slack thread: #cs-signal-lab (search: "fallback" Feb 2027)
- Confluence seed: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Signal-Lab-Index
- Example ticket (anonymized): JIRA-1234

If you want a condensed one-pager for exec: I can extract P0 items + ask for 2-week runway. Otherwise this doc should be enough for sprint planning.

-- Priya
